title: What to Donate, Sell, Store, Recycle, or Throw Away
subtitle: The out box is full and the sort is nearly done. Send each thing out through one of five doors, lean hard on the fast ones, and get it out of the house today.
part_position: Fourth and final chapter of Part Three (Sort), chapters 8 to 11; this chapter closes Sort
follows: Chapter 10 (Red Tags, Holding Areas, and Sorter's Remorse)
hands_off_note: Chapter 12 opens Part Four (Straighten); Sort is finished and only the keepers remain, and the next part stops removing and starts arranging.
audience: Readers at the end of a Sort pass who have already decided what is unnecessary and filled the out box, and now need to get it out of the house. Busy home keepers and parents. Applying the method, not new to it. They do not need another round of deciding; they need to route what is already decided, cleanly and without guilt.
core_promise: Route an already-decided out box through five doors, Donate, Sell, Store, Recycle, or Throw, with a quick cascade that picks each item's door in a second, a deliberate lean on the two fast lanes (Donate and Recycle), and guardrails that keep Sell and Store from quietly becoming permanent; then carry the whole box out in a single trip and finish Sort.
emotional_purpose: Make the last step of Sort feel light rather than fraught. Remove the guilt that clings to each door: donating is not waste, nobody has to sell anything, and throwing a worn-out thing away is not the failure the feeling insists it is, because the waste, if there ever was any, happened at the store. Deliver the honest milestone of the first S finished without overselling it.
practical_purpose: Draw the line between deciding a thing is unnecessary (already done) and deciding where it goes (today's only job); name the five doors and the quick routing cascade; make Donate the default for anything still usable; put a guardrail on each slow door (a sell-by deadline on Sell, a label and date on Store, and never rent space for what you do not need); reframe Recycle and Throw as the easy doors for the worn and finished; walk a short routing pass over the entryway out box; and read the friction meter as its last Sort step to a Sort-complete milestone.
primary_cta: Grab three things from the out box and get them out of the house today. The usable ones into a donation bag in your car; the broken one to recycling or the bin. Three things gone for good in five minutes. Read the chapter free in the online book.
secondary_cta: Read the chapter free online, then continue to Chapter 12, where Part Four begins and every keeper, still sitting where it landed, finally gets a place of its own so the space you cleared stays easy to keep.

worked_example.space: the entryway out box, tipped out and routed item by item down the cascade
worked_example.note: The whole box splits cleanly between the two fast doors, Donate and Recycle. Nothing was valuable enough to sell and nothing was needed later enough to store, which is the normal shape of an out box and exactly why Donate and Recycle are the lanes the cascade leans on.

items.two_extra_umbrellas: Perfectly good, just not needed (you do not need three); not worth the errand of selling, not needed later, still useful to someone, so Donate, into the bag.
items.surplus_tote_bags: Usable, not worth selling, not needed later, useful to plenty of people, so Donate; the few that are torn or stained are useful to no one, so those step over to Recycle.
items.spare_key_to_the_sold_car: Opens nothing, worth nothing, usable by no one; it fails every question until the last, so it takes the bottom of the cascade as scrap metal, Recycle if the program takes small metal or Throw if not, a two-second call.
items.old_takeout_menus: Paper, plain and simple, so Recycle.
items.dead_charging_cable: E-waste, so the electronics drop-off rather than the landfill, which is Recycle as well.

worked_example.tally: Two umbrellas and a handful of tote bags through Donate. Menus, a dead cable, some torn bags, and a useless key through Recycle, with the key allowed to Throw if that is simpler. Nothing sold, nothing stored, and the box left the house in one trip.

definition: Routing the out box means sending each unnecessary thing out through one of five doors, Donate, Sell, Store, Recycle, or Throw, and choosing the door that actually gets it gone. Donate and Recycle are the fast lanes and take most of the box; Sell and Store are the slow doors, worth it only for the rare item that truly earns them.
one_idea_to_keep: The best destination is the one that actually empties the box. A thing given away today beats a thing you mean to sell someday. Choose the door that gets it out of the house, and Sort is finished.

the bias is deliberate and strong: Donate and Recycle are the fast lanes and take most of the box; Sell and Store are narrow on purpose
Donate is the default because it is the exit that actually completes, same day, with nothing left to do

the sell trap: selling turns clearing into a part-time job, so sell only what is worth the work, with a sell-by date, and donate whatever has not sold
the store trap: storing is not deciding, so store only what you will truly use later, labeled and dated, and never rent space for what you do not need
Recycle is the second fast lane, for the worn and the electronic; do the responsible thing where it is easy
